nodes.label: reEncryptObjectStorage
nodes.rationale: Lists every object under keyPrefix; already at the active version means skip with no PUT, otherwise decrypt with the matching retired key and rewrite under the active one. Returns { scanned, rewrote, skippedCurrent, skippedUnencrypted, skippedNonAts1 } — the counts are the source of truth, there is no separate 'list stragglers' helper.

nodes.label: Online master-key rotation flow
nodes.rationale: Generate the new key as active with the old under retired, roll out, run the sweep, wait the rollback window (~7 days, because backups may still reference the old key), then drop the retired entry. Zero downtime and old data stays readable throughout.

nodes.label: Every key version is used once
nodes.rationale: One manifest byte is all a reader has to identify the key with, so two entries claiming the same version are refused at registration, at the store and at the start of a sweep. Without the check the lookup resolves the collision by precedence — active first — so payloads written under the older key are decrypted with the newer one and fail with an authentication-tag error that names nothing. The 32-byte length is checked in the same pass, since a short retired key is otherwise invisible until some payload at that version is read.

nodes.label: 255 is not a lifetime budget
nodes.rationale: It bounds how many versions may be live in one corpus at once, not how often you may rotate: a completed sweep puts every payload on the active version, the retired entries go away, and every other number is free again. From version 240 registration warns. There is deliberately no wider version field, because the sweep already resolves the only situation one would help with.

nodes.label: Keyring-completeness pre-check
nodes.rationale: The sweep samples the first encrypted objects and refuses to start if any payload's key version is missing from the keyring — catching 'operator dropped the retired key too soon' before a mid-sweep decrypt failure leaves the corpus half-rewritten.

nodes.label: InMemoryReEncryptProgressStore
nodes.rationale: A plain re-run re-lists and re-checks every key, which is fine for small buckets; a progress store lets a crashed sweep over a million-object corpus resume near where it stopped.

nodes.label: Rotating the HKDF context (newInfo)
nodes.rationale: Bodies are decrypted under info and rewritten under newInfo. Because the context is not in the manifest the sweep cannot tell a converted body from an unconverted one by reading the header, so while newInfo differs the version fast-path is switched off and every object is decrypted — a full read pass rather than a header scan. Without that, a context-only rotation would report everything as skipped-current and change nothing.

nodes.label: Sweep writes with an ETag compare-and-set
nodes.rationale: If the app wrote a newer version of an object the sweep is rewriting, the CAS fails, the sweep throws ObjectStorageConcurrencyError and aborts. Per-object failures are never swallowed; fix and re-run, since already-rewritten objects are idempotently skipped.
